transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I came in because I’m just so tired. Like, I can barely get through a shift at work, and I’m on my feet at the register trying to smile at people buying gum and lottery tickets, and it feels like my whole body is filled with wet sand. I’ll rest, or sit down when I can, but it doesn’t really bring me back. It’s just… heavy all the time.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it sad exactly. I mean… some days I’m just worn out, and that makes everything feel kind of gray, I guess. But “sad most of the time” is hard to say. Like, I’ll be at work and somebody will complain about the price of cigarettes, and I’m just standing there thinking about how the lights are too bright, and then I forget what mood I’m even in. So… I’m not sure.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like?

Yeah… I think so. Like, I used to really like cooking for myself, trying little recipes, even if it was just pasta with too much garlic, and now I’ll open the fridge and just stare at stuff like it belongs to someone else. And my guitar’s just sitting there—my brother actually asked if I was still playing, because he remembers when I’d bring it to family stuff, and then my aunt would ask me to play the same song every time, which got annoying but kind of sweet…

But now it all just feels flat. Hiking, going over to my family’s place, even things I usually love—I feel like I’m pretending to care more than actually enjoying it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah… sleep’s been weird. With my shifts changing around at the store, I got into this thing where I’d only sleep a few hours and somehow still feel wired, like I should be up reorganizing the kitchen or checking my phone or something. And now even when I’m exhausted, I’ll wake up really early and my mind is already going—like it starts before I’m even fully awake.
Do you often feel guilty about things?

Yeah… a lot, actually. I keep thinking I’ve let everybody down. Like my manager, if I mess something up at the register, I’ll replay it over and over like, see, that’s proof I’m no good at this. Even if it’s just a small mistake.

And then I think about my family, my little nieces… I don’t know, they’re kids, they don’t even know half of what I’m worried about, but I still feel like I’m failing them somehow. It kind of spirals.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in?

Not really… I mean, I try. I’ll make myself pick up the guitar sometimes, or I’ll think, okay, cook something decent instead of just standing there staring at the cabinet, but it’s like the feeling doesn’t show up.

Even hiking, which I used to love—there’s this one trail with the little creek, and my cousin slipped there once and we still tease her about it—but now I’m just… there. Same with going to my family’s place. I can laugh at the right time, I can act like I’m into it, but inside it all feels kind of flat, like I’m pretending to care.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. It’s like the things I normally like still exist, but they don’t really reach me anymore. Cooking for myself, playing guitar, hiking… even going over to my family’s place, which used to make me feel kind of grounded.

Now I’ll do it and it’s just flat. Like I’m going through the motions, smiling or nodding when I’m supposed to, but inside I’m kind of pretending to care.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… I think it’s been about four months? The low, empty part, I mean. It kind of kept going after that first rush I had at work passed, like when I was feeling all charged up and everything seemed important there for a while.

And then it just… didn’t lift. I remember thinking maybe it was just a bad week, or maybe I was tired from work—because the store was doing this whole display change and everyone was cranky about it—but no, it’s been months now. Around four.
Have you had periods like this before in your life?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had bad stretches before, like everybody does, I guess… times where I didn’t want to do much or I’d get kind of stuck in my head.

But I don’t know if it was like this, exactly. It’s hard to separate, because I’ll think back and then I start remembering other stuff, like where I was living then, or what shift I had at work, or some fight with my sister, and then I lose the thread.

So… maybe? But I can’t really say for sure.
Have you ever felt this way for an extended period before and then gotten better?

I don’t know… I’m trying to think of one, and it’s like my brain keeps pulling up random pieces instead of the actual answer.

Like I remember one winter where I barely went out, but that might’ve just been because it was freezing and my old apartment had this awful draft by the window, and I was working these weird shifts, so everything felt off anyway. And then maybe it got better when spring came? But I can’t tell if that was the same kind of feeling or just normal life getting less annoying.

So… I guess I’m not sure. I can’t clearly point to a time where I felt exactly like this for a long time and then definitely got better.
Have you had more than one period like this in your life where you felt empty and lost interest in activities?

I don’t know if it’s been more than one time exactly… but right now, yeah, that empty thing is really there.

Like, things I usually love just feel… flat. Cooking for myself, playing guitar, going hiking, even going over to my family’s place—normally there’s at least something in me that wants to do those things. Now it feels like I’m sort of pretending to care, if that makes sense.

I’ll pick up the guitar and then just set it back down, or I’ll think about making food and end up staring at the cabinets. Sorry, I know you asked if it happened more than once—I’m not sure about before. I just know this time it’s like everything got the color taken out of it.
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt this way?

I’m not sure if it’s been more than one period, honestly. I keep trying to line it up in my head, but then I start thinking about, like, when I used to cook more or when I was playing guitar more, and it all gets kind of mixed together.

But right now, yes — it’s that same flat feeling. Things I usually love, like cooking for myself, playing guitar, hiking, even going to my family’s place… it all feels kind of empty. Like I’m doing the motions or pretending I care, but I don’t really feel it.
Have you had an episode like this before that lasted for a while and then went away on its own?

I’m not sure… I keep trying to think of one that lasted a while and then just lifted, but it’s hard to separate it out.

There were times where I wasn’t doing much and I felt kind of off, but then I start thinking maybe it was because work was bad, or the weather was awful, or I was just tired all the time. Like I remember buying this little planner once because I thought if I organized myself I’d feel better, and then I lost it under a pile of mail for weeks, which is kind of funny but also not really…

So I don’t know if that counts as an episode that went away on its own. I can’t really say for sure.
Have you ever felt this way before in your life?

I mean… maybe, but I’m having trouble remembering it clearly. Right now it’s definitely there — that flat feeling.

Like, I used to actually enjoy cooking for myself, or I’d sit with my guitar and lose track of time. Hiking too, or even just going over to my family’s place, there’d be some kind of pull to do it. Now it’s like… I know I’m supposed to care, so I kind of act like I do, but inside it just feels blank.

I’m sorry, I know you asked if it happened before. I just keep thinking about all the things I used to like, and how weird it is that they don’t feel like anything now.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt this same way before?

I don’t know if I can pin down a whole other period, like a clear before-and-after thing. What I can say is this feels familiar in the sense that… things I usually love just don’t land right now.

Cooking, playing guitar, hiking, even going to my family’s place — it’s like I know those are “my” things, but they feel flat. I’ll think about making something nice and then it just feels like a chore, or I’ll pick up the guitar and it’s like I’m pretending to be interested.

Sorry, I’m kind of circling it. I’m not sure about before, but right now that same empty, pretending-to-care feeling is definitely there.
Have you ever had an episode like this before that lasted for a while and then went away, only to come back again?

I’m not sure. I keep trying to make it into a pattern, like it came, went away, and then came back, but I don’t know if that’s really true or if I’m just trying to organize it because you’re asking.

I’ve had stretches where I felt kind of… not right, but then life was also happening, you know? Work gets monotonous, bills pile up, my apartment gets messy, and then I’ll spend a whole Sunday deciding I’m going to clean everything and somehow end up sorting old receipts from two years ago instead. So I don’t know if that counts as it “coming back.”

I guess I can’t really say I’ve noticed a clear episode before that went away and then returned. Right now is just the one I can actually point to.
Did you have an episode like this before that went away and then came back?

I really don’t know. I feel like I should be able to say, “yes, this happened before and then it got better,” but when I try to remember it, it’s all kind of mixed in with regular life stuff.

Like there were times I’d come home from work and just sit there with the TV on, not really watching it, but then other times I was just tired because my shift was long or someone was rude at the register all day, so I don’t know if that’s the same thing. And then you get used to certain moods, I guess, and they blend together.

So… I can’t honestly point to a clear episode that went away and came back. This one just feels like the one I’m aware of right now.
Did you have an episode like this before that went away and then came back?

I don’t think I can say that clearly. I keep wanting to give you a neat answer, but my memory of it is kind of… messy.

Like, I remember different weeks where I’d feel off, but then I’d also be dealing with work stuff or not sleeping great because the neighbor’s dog barks at, like, 2 a.m.—not that that answers your question, sorry. And sometimes I’ll think, “Was that an episode?” but then it feels like I’m just labeling normal bad patches after the fact.

So no, I haven’t really noticed a definite thing where it went away and then came back. I’m not sure.
Did you have an episode like this before that went away and then came back?

I don’t really have a clear example, no. I know I keep circling around that, but it’s like… when I try to remember, I just think of random periods where things felt weird or stressful, and then I start thinking about work schedules or whether I was sleeping badly because my upstairs neighbor walks around like he’s moving furniture at midnight.

So I don’t know if that was something that went away and came back, or just me having rough patches. I haven’t noticed a definite episode before this one.
Is this the first time you've felt this way for an extended period?

I’m not totally sure. It feels like this is the first time I’ve really paid attention to it being this… stretched out, I guess.

But then I start second-guessing myself, because there were times before where I felt off for a while, and I’d just blame it on work or not sleeping right or life being annoying. Like when you’re standing at a register all day and everyone’s in a mood, it kind of follows you home, you know?

So… I don’t know if it’s the first time, exactly. It’s the first time I’m sitting here talking about it like this.
